items.name: Mediator channel reversal, Mon 23 Nov: Iran summoned Qatar's charge d'affaires over a joint German-Qatari statement condemning Iranian attacks (Baghaei: 'surprising and regrettable'; ending fighting on all fronts 'was an integral part of any agreement' - his response to the Qatari PM's Washington visit); MP Ahmad Bakhshaesh Ardestani: Qatar 'could no longer serve as an effective mediator'; Qatari PM/FM Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani due to meet Rubio in Washington Mon 23 Nov (State Dept statement Sun); Baghaei: 'no decision to withdraw from the NPT had been communicated to the ministry', Iran 'would honor its obligations for as long as it remained a member'; the blockade is 'military aggression' and Iran is 'entitled under the UN Charter to take political, economic and military measures against it'; IRGC adviser: airstrikes are Washington's only military option

items.note: T3 negative within 48 hours of the Tehran visit: the Qatari channel is being publicly discounted in Tehran on the day Doha's PM sits with Rubio. The NPT line is a T2-adjacent reading (a withdrawal threat hedged, not made). No Omani or Turkish mediation surfaced in any fetched page.

items.name: Front widening, Sat 21 - Sun 22 Nov: IRGC says it struck two US Patriot air-defence radars at bases in Bahrain with missiles and drones (response to 'US drone incursions'); Bahrain says its defences intercepted 'a number of projectiles' and a civilian industrial facility caught fire, two injured (one Pakistani resident critical); 'renewed' Iranian attack reported Sun 22 Nov 12:23 (Khaleej); condemnations from Saudi ('heinous'), Qatar ('flagrant violation'), Kuwait, UAE, Egypt, Jordan, Arab League; US Embassy Bahrain warning (Gulf News 20:01); IRGC also claims an F-16 damaged over the Gulf Fri 20 Nov (CENTCOM: 'FALSE', all jets accounted for) and an MQ-1 Predator downed east of Hormuz Sun 22 Nov (CENTCOM no comment; follows the 21 Nov MQ-9 / Qeshm claims recorded 11-21); Iran unveils a dual liquid-fuel missile launcher (IRGC Aerospace's Mousavi: capabilities 'have expanded significantly')

items.note: T4: first claimed Iranian strike on US air-defence assets in Bahrain in this sequence; the Gulf-state condemnation chorus is the diplomatic cost. Dating conflict: ABC/AND place the Bahrain attack Sat 21 Nov, Khaleej reports Sunday items including a 'renewed' attack - one or two attacks unclear. Trump's Monday Truth Social ('more drones and missiles in the last week than any time in over a year') is the US read of the same week.

items.name: Houthi-Saudi front, Sat 21 - Sun 22 Nov: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claims a 'direct hit' on Saudi Aramco's Rabigh refinery (Sun 22 Nov, X) as stage one of a 'two-stage' operation (stage two: a radar at Wadi al-Dawasir); Saudi authorities 'have not confirmed any attacks on refineries' (Reuters); coalition intercepted a ballistic missile in 'the west of the kingdom', two drones toward Riyadh and the south, and a missile near Mecca Sunday; Sat 21 Nov early: 3 ballistic missiles toward Riyadh intercepted (AFP heard two explosions); Aramco and Sumitomo (Petro Rabigh partner) silent; unverified OSINT: ~80 km smoke plume / ~410 MW fire by MTG-I1 (not confirmed by any wire); Houthi media: Saudi strike on a Hodeidah telecom building killed 4, wounded 18 (Mon 23 Nov)

items.note: Oil-relevant T4: Rabigh is a Red Sea-coast export refinery (west of the kingdom, outside Hormuz); a confirmed hit would be the first refinery damage claim of the sequence with production impact - none confirmed. Prior Rabigh claims 25 and 29 Oct were never confirmed. Monday's Asian oil trade cited the claim as the main upside driver (Reuters/BR).

items.name: Blockade test: Iranian hardliners push a tanker convoy from Kharg - Al-Monitor (20 Nov): more than 14 Iranian tankers gathered near Kharg Island, most with transponders off; Hamshahri (20 Nov): 14 tankers positioned; Fars urges a convoy; Ardabil prayer leader: tankers 'would soon set sail from Kharg for China'; Araghchi to ILNA (Fri 20 Nov): 'The blockade must be broken'; Friday prayer leader Haj-Aliakbari: 'If they want to test us, they can go ahead and test us'; Gulf News 22 Nov: 'Iran is preparing to send 14 oil tankers through the US naval blockade'; UANI's Charlie Brown: 'farcical', 'most likely propaganda', satellite imagery shows no significant loading at Kharg 'in quite some time'; ISW (20 Nov): Iran could try to break the blockade within days; Euronews 22 Nov: conflicting reports an Iranian tanker left Kharg Sunday; no Iranian official has confirmed a convoy; Mehr 'Iran dismisses reports' (ROBOTS_UNREACHABLE, not read)

items.note: late:true - the Al-Monitor/Hamshahri reports are 20 Nov and the Iran International piece 21 Nov 02:29Z, before this run's 12:11Z gate but inside tolerance and not in the 11-20/11-21 files (grep 'Kharg' empty). M-panel: a blockade-breaking attempt is the maritime-regime test the T panel cannot pre-empt; Trump's 'bottom of the sea' dare (22 Nov) is the US answer. Status as of 23 Nov 12Z: not sailed/not stopped in any fetched source; the 22 Nov UKMTO 'military forces' incident near Chabahar is the only candidate contact.

items.name: Maritime regime, 21-23 Nov: fifth and sixth Khasab-sequence hull hits Sat 21 Nov (UKMTO 215-26 ~0500Z stern, 11 nm N Khasab; 216-26 ~0550Z engine room, 17 nm E Khasab; both outbound, no casualties, unnamed) then a change of wording Sun 22 Nov: UKMTO 'incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman' east of the strait near Chabahar - the first 'military forces' advisory of the sequence; IRGC/Artesh claim 'two more supertankers' mined north of Al Ghanam the same morning; hormuz.now crossings collapse to 2 on Sun 22 Nov from 14 on Sat; CNN (via straits.live): Iranian attacks in the strait at the highest level since the conflict began; Lewis Pugh completes a protest swim of the strait (Guardian, 21 Nov, unconfirmed)

items.note: M-panel reading pair: attack tempo (3 UKMTO advisories in ~27 hours 20-21 Nov, then a 'military forces' incident) and flow response (14 -> 2 crossings). Whether the 22 Nov incident is US interdiction of an Iranian tanker (Euronews inference) or another Iranian strike is unresolved in every fetched page; it is the single most consequential open fact in this file.

items.note: O-panel: a weekend of six hull hits, a Patriot-site strike, a refinery claim and a convoy threat moved Brent by less than USD 1 either way and the prompt spread narrowed - the risk premium is not re-pricing on kinetic headlines; it is the equity rout (Friday) and the IEA ~2 mb/d surplus that the market is trading. Weekly: three straight losses. Trump (Mon 23 Nov Truth Social): oil 'dropped by a record level' since the election.
